claims.text: A microservice is a service (a program run as its own process, not a service-layer class) deployed and run on its own, owning one bounded context's data, reached only over the network, never by a method call or a shared table; it is not defined by its size in lines of code.
claims.source_hint: design judgement; glossary microservice; outline item 1, misconception 3

claims.text: A call between processes over the network can be slow or fail, and a caller that gets no answer (e.g. a timeout) cannot tell whether the other side did the work.
claims.source_hint: general networking; .NET docs: HttpClient.Timeout (request cancelled client-side, server may have processed it)

claims.text: At stage-2 QueuedNotifier.Send(Order order, string subject) implements INotifier, takes DonHangDbContext, and only calls db.Notifications.Add with Order = order, Status pending; it does not save (comment: saving is left to OrderService).

At stage-2 OrderService.PlaceOrderAsync calls notifier.Send(order, "order placed") then one repository.SaveChangesAsync; CancelOrderAsync and ShipOrderAsync likewise call notifier.Send then SaveChangesAsync.

EF Core with a relational provider: by default SaveChanges/SaveChangesAsync applies all tracked changes in one database transaction; if any command fails, the transaction is rolled back and none of the changes is applied.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Saving Data > Transactions (default transaction behavior)

claims.text: A PostgreSQL transaction runs in the session (connection) that began it; another process works on its own connection, so without an external transaction manager coordinating both, the two processes' saves commit separately.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL docs: 3.4 Transactions; BEGIN (transaction in the current session)

claims.text: Setting a navigation (Notification.Order = order) to a not-yet-saved entity lets EF Core fill in the foreign key (order_id) when it saves both in one SaveChanges (comment at QueuedNotifier.cs line 16).
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Changing Foreign Keys and Navigations; Saving related data (adding a graph of new entities); examples/don-hang @ stage-2: QueuedNotifier.cs:16

claims.text: At stage-2 NotificationQueue.ClaimDueAsync loads claimed rows with .Include(n => n.Order!).ThenInclude(o => o.Customer) (line 28) through DonHangDbContext.
EF Core: Include/ThenInclude load the related entities together with the queried entities as part of the query (eager loading).
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Loading Related Data > Eager Loading

claims.text: At stage-2 NotificationSender.SendOneAsync builds the email from customer.Email, customer.FullName (customer = notification.Order!.Customer!), notification.OrderId and notification.Subject; Notification.OrderId and Subject map to notifications.order_id and subject.
At stage-2 NotificationSender is a BackgroundService running inside the api process, beside the requests.
git show <tag>:<path> prints the content of that file as it is at the tag.

Before a module runs as a separate service, each shared object, transaction and table read must become data it receives and keeps (an order id may stay as a plain value); inside one process that is a refactoring, after the split each side must work with the other's old and new version.
Size can still matter when one team must understand and own a whole service (opposing view to 'not defined by size').
When a method's signature or a type changes, the C# compiler reports an error at every caller that no longer compiles; a change in meaning that still compiles is not reported.
claims.source_hint: C# language: compile-time overload resolution and type checking (compiler errors such as CS1501, CS7036, CS1503)

claims.text: At stage-2 a migration adds a foreign key FK_notifications_orders_order_id from notifications.order_id to orders.id; DonHangDbContext maps HasOne(n => n.Order).WithMany().HasForeignKey(n => n.OrderId).

In ClaimDueAsync, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED is in raw SQL selecting from notifications alone (EF Core composes the Include over it as a subquery), so it row-locks only notifications rows, inside the transaction begun at line 18.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL docs: SELECT > The Locking Clause; EF Core docs: SQL Queries > Composing with LINQ; NotificationQueue.cs:16-30 @ stage-2
